union.summary: Unrequested semantic change to ALL bounded-range aggregations: `Arguments.iterate` now silently skips blank cells for every range reference, not just unbounded ones
union.evidence: packages/sheets/src/formula/arguments.ts: `const isRange = isSrng(node.v); for (const ref of toSrefs([node.v])) { if (isRange) { const cell = grid.get(ref); if (!cell || cell.v === undefined || cell.v === '') continue; } ... }`. The issue only asks for whole-column/row/open-ended lexing + evaluation; this changes the meaning of existing formulas such as `=AVERAGE(A1:A10)` or `=COUNT`/`=MIN`/`=MAX` over a partially-empty bounded range. Worse, the design doc presents it as pre-existing behavior — docs/design/sheets/formula.md: "Blank cells inside a range contribute nothing to aggregations (`Arguments.iterate` skips them)" — so the doc does not record that a cross-cutting evaluation-semantics change was made here. If blank-skipping is genuinely required for `AVERAGE(B2:B)` = 200, that should be stated as an intentional, documented semantics change with its own note in the design doc.

union.summary: `Store.getUsedBounds()` added as a required interface method but possibly not implemented by every Store implementation (IDBStore)
union.evidence: packages/sheets/src/store/store.ts adds `getUsedBounds(): Promise<Range | undefined>;` to the `Store` interface (non-optional). Implementations are added only for MemStore, ReadOnlyStore and YorkieStore. packages/sheets/src/store/memory.ts still carries the comment "Unlike the `IDBStore` implementation, this builds the map from the entire grid", indicating at least one other Store implementation (and any test doubles/mocks implementing `Store`) exists that was not updated. The plan doc itself scopes this to "3 impls" (docs/tasks/active/20260722-open-ended-ranges-todo.md: "`Store.getUsedBounds()` + 3 impls"), so an IDBStore/other implementation would be left non-conforming.

union.summary: The issue's literal acceptance scenario (D1–D5 formulas in one sheet) is not demonstrated and likely does not produce the stated numbers, because expansion uses whole-sheet used bounds
union.evidence: The issue fixes a single setup (A1=10,A2=20,A3=30,B1=100,B2=200) and expects D1..D5 to yield 60/110/200/5/360 simultaneously. `resolveRange` fills omitted columns from `Store.getUsedBounds()`, which is the bounding box of *all* populated cells including the D-column formula cells. With all five formulas present, `=SUM(1:1)` in D2 expands to `A1:D1` (D1 = 60) → 170, and `=SUM(1:3)` in D5 expands to `A1:D3` → 360 + D1 + D2 + D3. packages/sheets/test/sheet/calculation.test.ts sidesteps this by constructing `new Sheet(new MemStore())` per case and placing only one formula. Related unspecified case: a whole-column formula placed *inside* the referenced column (e.g. `=SUM(A:A)` in A5) becomes self-referential once bounds include the formula cell — neither the design doc nor the tests state the intended behavior (Excel raises a circular-reference error).

union.summary: Newly lexable unbounded refs are not integrated with existing reference-rewriting machinery (`shiftFormula`/`shiftSref`, autofill/copy-paste adjustment)
union.evidence: packages/sheets/src/index.ts exports `shiftSref`, `shiftFormula`, `shiftDimensionMap`, which rewrite REFERENCE tokens when rows/columns are inserted or deleted. After this grammar change, `A:A`, `1:1`, `A1:B` lex as REFERENCE tokens and will flow into those code paths, which parse endpoints with the full-ref assumption (`parseRef`). Neither the diff nor docs/design/sheets/formula.md mentions how unbounded refs survive row/column insert-delete, fill-handle, or copy/paste reference adjustment; only `extractFormulaRanges` is called out as a limitation. A partially-supported syntax that corrupts on structural edits is a fit gap for the feature.

union.summary: Formula range highlighting silently does not support the newly accepted syntax
union.evidence: docs/design/sheets/formula.md (new text): "Whole-column/row highlighting (`extractFormulaRanges`) skips unbounded refs." `extractFormulaRanges` is described in the same doc as "Returns ranges referenced in the formula ... for visual highlighting". A user typing `=SUM(A:A)` gets no highlight, unlike every other range form — a user-visible inconsistency introduced by, and belonging to, this feature. It is documented rather than fixed; acceptable only if deliberately deferred (and it should then be a tracked follow-up, not just a doc sentence).

union.summary: Reference parsing is re-implemented rather than reused; the lexer's REF rule is duplicated as a hand-written regex that can drift from the grammar
union.evidence: packages/sheets/src/model/core/coordinates.ts adds `parsePartialRef` (`cleaned.match(/^([A-Za-z]*)([0-9]*)$/)`) and `isFullRef` (`/^\$?[A-Za-z]+\$?[0-9]+$/`). The file already contains `parseRef`, `parseRange`, `parseColumnLabel` and `toRange`; the new regexes restate the `COL`/`ROW` fragments just introduced in packages/sheets/antlr/Formula.g4 in a second, unrelated dialect (e.g. the regex accepts unlimited letters where COL caps at 3, and accepts a leading `0` row where ROW requires `[1-9]`). A single shared column/row parser (or deriving from the grammar fragments) would keep the two definitions from diverging.

union.summary: Expansion must be manually re-applied at every dependants-map site (1 in MemStore, 3 in YorkieStore, 1 in calculator); no shared helper, so the frontend package now duplicates evaluation-layer knowledge
union.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-store.ts wraps `extractReferences(cell.f)` with `expandUnboundedRanges(cell.f, bounds)` in three separate blocks; packages/sheets/src/store/memory.ts does the same a fourth time; packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/calculator.ts a fifth. The pre-existing duplication of `buildDependantsMap` is amplified rather than factored — a single exported helper (e.g. `extractDependencies(formula, bounds)`) would be the natural reuse point and would guarantee any future Store implementation cannot forget the rewrite.

union.summary: Bounds are recomputed per formula cell by scanning the whole index, and whole-column ranges materialize the full data extent through `fetchGridByReferences`
union.evidence: packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/calculator.ts calls `await sheet.getUsedBounds()` inside the per-cell calculation loop, and packages/sheets/src/store/cell-index.ts `bounds()` iterates every key of `rowIndex` and `colIndex` on each call (no cached/incrementally maintained min/max). Combined with expanding `A:A` to the full used extent before `fetchGridByReferences`, this makes whole-column formulas O(rows) per evaluation and bounds O(R+C) per formula cell. For a spreadsheet engine this is a layer/approach concern worth stating in the design doc's trade-offs section, which currently discusses only correctness.

The issue lists only whole-column, whole-row and open-ended column shapes. Accepting extra non-standard syntax widens the supported language beyond the spec with no documented semantics.

per_sample.summary: Wrong-layer approach: unbounded ranges are handled by string-rewriting the formula (tokenize → splice → re-lex) rather than resolving at the AST/reference-resolution layer, and the endpoint parsing is re-implemented with a regex instead of reusing existing ref parsing
per_sample.evidence: packages/sheets/src/formula/formula.ts `expandUnboundedRanges` rebuilds the formula text (`body += toSrng(resolveRange(...))`, `return '=' + body`) so it must be re-lexed by every downstream consumer, and packages/sheets/src/model/core/coordinates.ts adds `parsePartialRef` with its own `/^([A-Za-z]*)([0-9]*)$/` regex plus `isFullRef` `/^\$?[A-Za-z]+\$?[0-9]+$/`, duplicating the `$`-stripping/column-label logic that `parseRef`/`parseRange` already own. The `try { ... } catch { /* fall through */ }` in `expandUnboundedRanges` silently degrades to the unexpanded (error-producing) formula, hiding layering failures.

per_sample.summary: The "expand then extract dependencies" step is copy-pasted across store implementations instead of being a single shared helper, inviting divergence (and a missed call site is exactly how a backend loses the feature)
per_sample.evidence: packages/sheets/src/store/memory.ts (`toSrefs(extractReferences(expandUnboundedRanges(cell.f, bounds)))`) and packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-store.ts repeat the identical wrapping three separate times inside `buildDependantsMap`, which is why `expandUnboundedRanges` had to be added to the public barrel in packages/sheets/src/index.ts. A shared `extractDependencies(formula, bounds)` in @wafflebase/sheets would keep the rule in one place, consistent with the repo's stated reuse expectation.

per_sample.summary: Self-reference/circularity of whole-column ranges is neither specified nor handled: a `=SUM(A:A)` written inside column A expands to a range containing its own cell
per_sample.evidence: packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/calculator.ts expands `cell.f` against `sheet.getUsedBounds()`, which includes the formula cell itself once written. Every test in packages/sheets/test/sheet/calculation.test.ts places the formula in column D (`{ r: 1, c: 4 }`), so the in-column case is undefined behavior; docs/design/sheets/formula.md's new section does not state the intended semantics (Excel reports a circular reference) nor list it as a non-goal.

per_sample.summary: Cross-sheet unbounded refs now lex successfully but evaluate to `#ERROR!` — the grammar advertises a syntax the engine cannot honour, a gap accepted only in prose
per_sample.evidence: packages/sheets/antlr/Formula.g4 lets `REFERENCE: SHEET_NAME '!' REFRANGE` match `Sheet2!A:A`, while formula.ts `expandUnboundedRanges` explicitly skips `isCrossSheetRef(token.text)` and docs/design/sheets/formula.md records "Cross-sheet unbounded refs (`Sheet2!A:A`) are not resolved ... and evaluate to `#ERROR!`". Widening the lexer without a resolution path yields a syntactically valid formula that always errors; the issue does not request cross-sheet support, so narrowing the grammar (or resolving it) would fit the spec better.

per_sample.summary: `getUsedBounds()` is recomputed per formula cell during recalculation instead of once per pass
per_sample.evidence: packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/calculator.ts calls `await sheet.getUsedBounds()` inside the per-cell calculation loop, and `CellIndex.bounds()` scans all row and column index keys on each call; hoisting it out of the loop would match the design doc's framing that clamping "happens up front".
